queries: WITH c AS (SELECT archstat, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM scanqc GROUP BY archstat), s AS (SELECT archstat, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT archstat, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT archstat, cnt AS record_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_above_average FROM a WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY share DESC

assumptions.assumption: A NULL archstat is its own group; GROUP BY puts NULLs in one group, so it is counted and included in the average share.
'How far above' means the absolute difference share - average share, not a ratio or percentage.
Share is a fraction from 0 to 1, not a percentage. It is unrounded. The average share is the mean of the per-status shares, which equals 1 / number of statuses.

assumptions.assumption: Missing archstat (NULL) is its own group, and GROUP BY keeps NULL as one group. Empty strings are treated as ordinary distinct values, not missing.
The average share is the unweighted mean of the per-status shares, taken over all groups including the NULL group. This equals 1 divided by the number of groups.
'How far above' means the absolute difference share - avg_share, not a ratio or percentage.
